title: Correct landing distance
description: Essential: The final answer for part (1) must be correctly calculated as √3 m or approximately 1.732 m.

title: Correct power value
description: Essential: The final answer for part (2) must be correctly calculated as (15/2)√5 W or approximately 16.77 W.

title: Projectile motion setup
description: Important: The student must correctly apply kinematic equations to find the flight time from the drop height and the horizontal displacement from the initial velocity.

title: Initial velocity relation
description: Important: The student must correctly relate the angular velocity to the linear velocity at the table edge using v₀ = ωR.

title: Tension force analysis
description: Important: The student must resolve the tension force, apply Newton's second law for circular motion (T cosθ = m v₀²/R), and identify the correct geometry (sinθ = r/R).

title: Power calculation method
description: Important: The student must correctly apply the power formula P = F ⋅ v, using the component of tension perpendicular to the velocity (P = T v₀ sinθ).

title: Distance geometry
description: Optional: The student may correctly use the 3D Pythagorean theorem (s = √(R² + x² + h²)) to find the distance from the landing point to center O.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: The student's working shows consistent use of SI units (m, s, kg, rad/s) throughout the calculation.

title: Incorrect radius for velocity
description: Pitfall: Using the turntable radius (r) instead of the tabletop radius (R) to calculate the initial linear velocity (v₀ = ωr).

title: Power component error
description: Pitfall: Using the wrong component of tension or velocity in the power calculation (e.g., P = T v₀ or P = T v₀ cosθ).
